study_design: Randomized chemoprevention study among patients with high-grade prostate intraepithelial neoplasia, with one year of follow-up.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 40 patients with HGPIN were randomized into 2 groups: one received 4 mg lycopene twice a day for one year, and the other was periodically followed up.
reason: The study evaluates development of occult prostate cancer among patients with HGPIN. HGPIN is a precursor lesion and does not establish an aggressive prostate cancer endpoint; the resulting occult prostate cancer endpoint is general incidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Our results show that lycopene can delay or prevent HGPIN from developing into occult prostate cancer, and there exists an inverse relationship between lycopene and prostate-specific antigen.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row concerns prevention of newly developing occult prostate cancer, not high-grade, advanced, metastatic, or lethal prostate cancer incidence.
